newsitem.title: USA: Compaq Q2 margins up, sees strong 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: Compaq Q2 margins up, sees strong 2nd half.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp said Thursday its second quarter gross profit margin rose to 25.3 percent from 24.5 percent in the first quarter, and it continues to expect a strong second half.

Compaq reported second quarter net income of $422 million, or $1.48 a share, excluding a one-time charge of $208 million, or $0.73 a share, for purchased technology in connection with its acquisition of Microcom.
The First Call consensus estimate was $1.39 a share.
Compaq earned $0.96 a share diluted in the 1996 second quarter.
Including the second-quarter charge, Compaq reported net income of $214 million, or $0.75 a share diluted.

Compaq said it is implementing the first phase of a new manufacturing and distribution model, called build-to-order, that will result in substantial customer benefits, accelerate its market share gains and improve profitability.
Later this morning Compaq is expected to unveil corporate desktop PCs, as well as price cuts, that are its first products designed using its new manufacturing method.
Compaq said its build-to-order strategy will shorten its manufacturing cycle time, improve product availability and predictability, reduce channel inventory, and cut product costs.
The company said it ended the second quarter with a cash balance of $5.1 billion, including cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments.
Compaq said its cash increased as a result of operational improvements and asset management such as its increased inventory turns and fewer sales days outstanding.
